precepts.text: The priests were arrayed in long garments; old history of the garments ordained for the men.
precepts.point: The sealed of the Lord receive the same. The hundred forty and four thousand of Revelation 7 that must be sealed before destruction comes are read of again in 2 Esdras: they departed from the shadow of the world, leaving spiritual Egypt and the ways Babylon taught behind, and have received glorious garments of the Lord. In the kingdom of heaven the Most High will clothe His men in glorious garments as in ancient times, on another level than anything worn today.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

precepts.why:
Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar were taken from among the children of Israel to minister in the priest’s office, and the Most High commanded “holy garments for Aaron thy brother for glory and for beauty.” Here is old history of those garments: the priests were set “according to their daily courses, being arrayed in long garments, in the temple of the Lord.”

Garments were ordained for the men of Israel. When the world hears Deuteronomy 22:5 and asks why the men wear garments, the answer is here: the most holy and regarded men of the nation, the priests, were arrayed in long garments down to the foot.

precepts.text: In the days of Josias the feast of unleavened bread is called the feast of sweet bread, kept seven days with the passover.
precepts.point: On the last day of unleavened bread you may also cook, unless it falls on the seventh day Sabbath. The only time you can cook on the seventh day Sabbath is when the Passover falls on that day, because you cannot have the Passover without the lamb roast with fire; no other high holy day gives you a set meal, and no other feast overrides the Sabbath cooking prohibition.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
In the days of king Josias the feast has another name: “the children of Israel which were present held the passover at that time, and the feast of sweet bread seven days.” The feast of sweet bread is the feast of unleavened bread, kept seven days with the passover, just as Leviticus 23 sets it: “seven days ye must eat unleavened bread.”

On the last day of unleavened bread you may also cook, unless it falls on the seventh day Sabbath. The only time you can cook on the seventh day Sabbath is when the Passover falls on that day, because you cannot have the Passover without the lamb roast with fire. No other high holy day gives you a set meal, and no other feast overrides the Sabbath cooking prohibition.

precepts.text: Josiah put himself in the midst of a war the Most High had sent Pharaoh to fight, and it cost him his life; when the Lord is in the midst of a thing, it is best to get out of the way.
precepts.point: The reason is given: that the cruelty done to the threescore and ten sons of Jerubbaal might come, and their blood be laid upon Abimelech their brother, which slew them, and upon the men of Shechem, which aided him in the killing of his brethren. The hired men and the backers carried the blood guilt too. Abimelech ran for three years and everything looked good, but you are not getting away with evil.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

precepts.why:
When the Lord is in the midst of a thing, it is best to get out of the way. “Pharaoh the king of Egypt came to raise war at Carchamis upon Euphrates: and Josias went out against him. But the king of Egypt sent to him, saying, What have I to do with thee, O king of Judea? I am not sent out from the Lord God against thee; for my war is upon Euphrates: and now the Lord is with me, yea, the Lord is with me hasting me forward: depart from me, and be not against the Lord.”

Josiah put himself in the midst of a war the Most High had sent Pharaoh to fight, and it cost him his life. The Most High is the one mustering these wars, and he was the one who sent the evil spirit between Abimelech and Shechem. When he stirs a war, he is in the midst of it.

precepts.text: Josiah held the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
precepts.point: Reading the book of the law brought the nation back to keeping the appointed feasts in order, just as the feast is kept in order today.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
“And Josias held the feast of the passover in Jerusalem unto his Lord, and offered the passover the fourteenth day of the first month.”

Josiah commanded all the people, “Keep the passover unto the Lord your God, as it is written in the book of this covenant”, and he kept it in its appointed time, the fourteenth day of the first month. Reading the book of the law brought the nation back to keeping the appointed feasts in order, just as the feast is kept in order today.

precepts.text: The magnitude of the offering showed how great and well ordered this Passover was.
precepts.point: Reading the book of the law brought the nation back to keeping the appointed feasts in order, just as the feast is kept in order today.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

precepts.why:
“And Jeconias, and Samaias, and Nathanael his brother, and Assabias, and Ochiel, and Joram, captains over thousands, gave to the Levites for the passover five thousand sheep, and seven hundred calves.”

The magnitude of the offering shows how great and well ordered this Passover was. “Surely there was not holden such a passover from the days of the judges that judged Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel, nor of the kings of Judah.”

precepts.text: How the temple and city were destroyed and a remnant carried into Babylon.
precepts.point: We are become a reproach to our neighbors, a scorn and a derision to them that are round about us. The neighbors in this context are the enemies, the other nations, the heathen. You know this because verse one already established that the heathen came in and defiled the temple, so the neighbors reproaching us are those same nations.

note.label: Psalm 79: The Heathen Have Defiled Thy Inheritance

precepts.why:
“O God, the heathen are come into thine inheritance; thy holy temple have they defiled; they have laid Jerusalem on heaps.” This is not a one-time thing. It happened when Babylon besieged us first, again during the time of the Greeks who destroyed our land, and again in 70 A.D. when we were pushed out of the land. During the Greeks not all of us were pushed out and taken captive in other nations like with Babylon and 70 A.D.

Esdras tells how the temple and city were destroyed by Babylon and a remnant carried away: “As for the house of the Lord, they burnt it, and brake down the walls of Jerusalem, and set fire upon her towers: And as for her glorious things, they never ceased till they had consumed and brought them all to nought: and the people that were not slain with the sword he carried unto Babylon: Who became servants to him and his children, till the Persians reigned, to fulfil the word of the Lord spoken by the mouth of Jeremy: Until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths, the whole time of her desolation shall she rest, until the full term of seventy years.”

Even during the time of kings, our forefather King Zedekiah was taken into captivity, he and his sons and daughters. A remnant was taken captive in Babylon, which is why Daniel was born there, and they destroyed the temple and the city. That is the heathen defiling the holy temple and laying Jerusalem on heaps, with the blood of his servants shed like water and none to bury them.
